matches.rationale: Both identify the same inconsistency: Table 2 shows 0.00±0.00 barrier for BookCorpus under learned matching, while Section 5 text states BookCorpus is an exception with non-zero barriers. This is the exact discrepancy described in gt_id 1.

Both identify that Equation 2 uses 'inf' (infimum) instead of 'sup' (supremum), which contradicts the barrier definition's objective to measure maximum deviation. The finding correctly notes this should be supremum for consistency with Equation 1.

The ground truth concerns overgeneralization in the Abstract about applicability to all Transformers without acknowledging RoPE limitations in Appendix F. The findings do not identify this specific cross-section issue about architectural constraints and RoPE models.

The ground truth identifies missing learning rate specification (η) for the alignment procedure in Algorithm 1. Finding 5 discusses a different issue about λ sampling not shown in pseudocode, not the missing learning rate hyperparameter.
The ground truth identifies a fabricated citation 'Zhou et al., 2024' that doesn't exist in the References section. None of the findings identify this specific missing or fabricated reference issue.

Both identify inappropriate promotional language in the Introduction/Abstract. Finding 1 quotes 'completely solve,' 'eliminates all limitations,' and 'perfect zero-barrier connectivity in all cases' as exaggerated claims, matching the rhetorical inflation described in gt_id 6.

The ground truth identifies that Equation 3 was changed from argmax to argmin, inverting the alignment objective. None of the findings identify this specific equation error or the contradiction in the optimization direction.

The ground truth identifies removal of nuanced discussion about BookCorpus higher barriers and possible explanations. While finding 6 notes a text-table inconsistency about BookCorpus, it doesn't identify the missing discussion of imperfect alignment vs. disconnected minima that gt_id 8 describes.

Both identify that the ⋄ operator used in Figure 2(b) for blockwise multiplication is never properly defined in the paper. Finding 9 notes it's only defined in external code, matching the undefined notation issue in gt_id 9.

The ground truth identifies misrepresentation of Figure 5, claiming weight matching shows 'perfect alignment' when it actually shows imperfect alignment with broadly distributed eigenangles. None of the findings identify this specific figure misinterpretation issue.

The ground truth identifies undisclosed temperature scaling applied to Tiny ImageNet in Appendix B.1 without clarifying if it was applied to other datasets/baselines. None of the findings identify this specific asymmetric preprocessing protocol issue.
The ground truth identifies removal of Appendix A (Limitations section) which violates transparency norms. None of the findings identify the missing limitations section or its removal.

Both identify misrepresentation of Figure 4. Finding 8 notes the text claims 'uniform color' and 'complete zero deviation' but the figure shows color variation, matching gt_id 13's identification of exaggerated claims about 'near-zero deviation' when the figure shows substantial positive deviations.

The ground truth identifies misattribution of Git Re-Basin to Singh and Jaggi [2020] instead of Ainsworth et al. [2022]. None of the findings identify this specific citation misattribution in the Related Work section.

Both identify the contradiction between Introduction (emphasizing need for symmetries beyond permutations) and Conclusion (claiming permutations alone are sufficient). Finding 2 explicitly quotes both sections showing this cross-section incoherence about the value of the framework.
